notes: Training objectives: Qwen RL = correctness only; LFM RL = correctness + tool-efficiency bonus. SFT = demonstration imitation.
Savings (%) = 100 × (1 − checkpoint tool calls / baseline tool calls), summing over the same task/harness pairs solved by both. Positive = fewer calls; negative = more.

Only native ATIF agent tool calls with valid unique IDs are counted. These are harness-level tool invocations, not shell subcommands or model turns. Missing trajectories are excluded and coverage is recorded.
Each checkpoint has its own matched successful subset. Per-harness sample counts are shown. Differences are descriptive; fewer calls alone do not establish better task performance.
Native OpenCode uses its own historical baseline (15.9%). Other Qwen runs use the Harbor baseline (14.6%). LFM baseline has 998 grades.
Incomplete evaluations (*) and test-overlap runs (†) retain those labels. RL best selection uses correctness, not tool efficiency. SFT does not optimize an explicit tool-efficiency reward.
